Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: prompt harvest & model-fit next steps (Acme Legal)

Hi Nora — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on so we keep momentum: 

- Goal: evaluate model fit for Acme Legal search assistant (prioritize recall for legal citations, high precision for relevancy).
- Immediate asks from our side: a small representative set (~200 rows) of real customer prompts (redacted as needed), edge-case queries, and 10 intentionally messy examples that break current ranking.
- What we’ll deliver: recommended model variants (3 tiers), benchmark summary (latency/cost/LLM-quality vs your evals), and an initial prompt-set for regressions.

Next steps I’m proposing (feel free to update):
1) You upload a CSV of prompts (we discussed a sample schema) or reply to this thread with a few examples — target by EOD Wed (Aug 20).
2) Internal: Laura & Vivek will run quick A/B model fits and share a short benchmark with suggested configs by Thu (Aug 21).
3) Follow-up 30 min call to review findings and next runway (provisioning Dedicated or Hosted path). I’ll send options — aiming for Fri morning PT.

Attached: prompt_collection_instructions.md — short template for redaction and CSV schema. Key note on PII: please replace names, client IDs, and any contract numbers with the token [REDACTED_ID] per our guidance. If you need us to accept an encrypted file (SFTP), let me know.

Thanks — excited to dig in.

—Sean

Two questions from our side:

Also looping in Samir from our search engineering team for any clarifications on the prompt columns.

Date: Thu, 21 Aug 2025 07:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: prompt harvest & model-fit next steps (Acme Legal)

Sean / Vivek — I pulled the CSV and ran a quick pass (220 rows looks great for an initial sweep). High-level notes: 

- Data quality: many short queries and several long multi-sentence fact-finding prompts — good coverage for prompt generalization. A few rows include contract excerpts; those should be redacted or hashed (Nora, thanks for the heads-up about keeping a mapping internally).
- Model recommendations (fast evaluation tier): open-weights quantized variants via dedicated hosted runtime are a good fit for latency-sensitive routes. Specifically: openlm-13B-q4 >> for a good balance of latency + citation precision.
- Quality tier (higher LR/citation fidelity): a finetuned 33B-class instruction model with KV-cache enabled; expect higher token cost but significantly fewer citation hallucinations in our benchmarks. We’ll include a candidate we tested (benchmark_summary.pdf).
- Safety/guardrails: add a citation-check step in the pipeline (rule: require source token overlap > 0.35 for system to surface legal citations; otherwise return a safe fallback response pointing to search results). We can prototype this as a post-filter during the eval run.

Attached a short benchmark_summary.pdf with throughput/latency/cost and a recommended config per route. Also attached prompt-redaction-guidelines.txt — same guidance Sean referenced.

Proposed next actions:
- We’ll run two A/B jobs (openlm-13B-q4 vs finetuned-33B) on your sample set and return a consolidated quality matrix by EOD Thu (Aug 21).
- Schedule the Friday sync to review the matrix + recommended rollout (will bring a solutions engineer).

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Nora — and huge thanks to Laura and Vivek for the quick turnaround.

Nora, to confirm next steps on our side:
- We’ll share the A/B matrix and a short slide (one pager) with recommended model variants and cost/latency tradeoffs by EOD today (see benchmark link above).
- We recommend a follow-up 30-min review on Fri Aug 22 at 10:00 AM PT — invite is on the way; please let me know if you’d prefer a different time.
- For PII mapping: yes, keeping the mapping internally on Acme’s side is fine; please ensure the CSV we ingest replaces IDs with [REDACTED_ID] and you store the mapping separately. If you’d prefer SFTP transfer, send SFTP details and we’ll get security sign-off.

Quick ask for the call: please have a technical search engineer (Samir) and your legal ops contact if possible — we’ll go over the citation guardrail approach and can show a failing example live.

Thanks all — looking forward to the review.
